headline: Alignment-free and offline tools advance viral variant detection from sequencing reads
label: Viral Genomics Inference Methods
summary: Read-level and offline pipelines now target viral variant calling, abundance estimation and genome recovery with reduced reliance on full alignment or exhaustive search.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these items is reducing the computational overhead of viral inference by operating directly on raw reads or spectra rather than on full alignment or exhaustive database search. bronko detects viral SNPs, indels and minor variants directly from reads without alignment, with near-linear scaling in sequencing depth. EMtrace provides an offline laptop pipeline for nanopore metagenomics that classifies reads, estimates abundance via expectation-maximisation, and assembles consensus genomes for viral diagnostics, genome recovery and 16S profiling. A saliva proteomics strategy applies a similar pruning logic, reducing viral search databases by 82-95% while keeping sensitivity through single amino acid variant detection. What is new is the explicit targeting of tractable inference at the read or spectrum level. The items differ in data modality, so this describes the dominant emphasis rather than a shared method.
